exploration.title: Circuit City
exploration.subject: Physics
exploration.summary: Compare one series path with parallel branches, then measure how voltage changes current, power and energy.
exploration.question: How do circuit paths and source voltage control charge flow and energy transfer?
exploration.explanation: Current is charge flow rate (A = C/s), voltage is energy transferred per charge (V = J/C), and power is energy-transfer rate (W = J/s). For each fixed 12 Ω resistor in this ideal direct-current model, V = IR and P = VI. The same current passes through every load in series, while parallel branch currents add at the source. Charge is conserved around a complete circuit; the source transfers energy to the loads. The model uses an ideal 0–18 V source, zero-resistance wires and fixed resistors. It omits heating, transients, source sag, component limits and protective devices and is not guidance for household mains wiring.

experiments.title: Open one switch
experiments.instruction: Predict the effect of opening house 2. Compare series and parallel at the same ideal 12 V source, with houses 1 and 3 closed and all three resistors fixed at 12 Ω.
experiments.observe: Series source current is 0 A because the only path is open. In parallel, houses 1 and 3 each carry 1 A and transfer 12 W while house 2 carries 0 A. Explain which paths remain complete.

experiments.title: Double the voltage
experiments.instruction: Predict what changes when the ideal source increases from 6 V to 12 V. Keep all switches closed, use parallel wiring, keep each resistor fixed at 12 Ω and observe both trials for 10 s.
experiments.observe: Each branch changes from 0.5 A, 3 W and 30 J to 1 A, 12 W and 120 J. Use I = V/R and P = V²/R to explain why current doubles while power and energy quadruple.

exploration.misconception: A load does not use up charge. Charge returns to the source while energy is transferred from the source to the loads; moving markers show conventional-current direction, not individual charges or their drift speed.
